findings.title: traceID dropped from the grafana-data-egress log line
findings.body: The old logRequest explicitly appended a traceID field (tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)) to the 'Plugin Request Completed' event. That code is removed in this PR, and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware/instrumentContext does not add a trace ID either. The egress event therefore no longer carries traceID, so plugin request logs can no longer be correlated with traces unless the infra logger injects trace IDs from ctx on its own, which this diff does not show. The event loses a field it previously always emitted when a trace was present.

findings.title: Moved egress-log fields have no test coverage and depend on implicit ordering
findings.body: instrumentContext now carries pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname that LoggerMiddleware used to emit directly. They reach the 'grafana-data-egress' event only if (a) ConcreteLogger.FromContext renders contextual attributes from ctx, and (b) ContextualLoggerMiddleware is ordered outside LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares. Nothing in this PR tests either condition: there is no unit test for ContextualLoggerMiddleware, and the existing metrics test no longer covers the enrichment it used to exercise. Reordering the middleware list or changing FromContext would silently strip plugin and datasource identifiers from the data-egress event with no failing test.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so its output is invisible to the test
findings.body: FromContext returns a brand-new NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now emits its only log line via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so messages go to a throwaway object and never reach the TestLogger's InfoLogs/ErrorLogs counters. Any test that uses plog.TestLogger to assert on the egress log will observe zero calls. Returning f, or sharing the Logs state, would keep the fake observable.

findings.title: FromContext silently discards context attributes when the type assertion fails
findings.body: If d.l.FromContext(ctx) does not return a *log.ConcreteLogger, the wrapper falls back to d.New(), which drops ctx entirely and logs nothing about the failure. The data-egress log now relies on FromContext to carry pluginId, endpoint, dsUID and similar fields, so this path would silently remove them from every plugin request log line. The fallback should preserve the attributes or surface the mismatch.

findings.title: FromContext doc comment is copied from New and misdescribes the method
findings.body: The comment 'returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context' is the New() description. FromContext takes a context.Context and derives its attributes from that context value, which the comment does not say. Callers implementing the interface are given a misleading contract.
